claims.claim: Goal: reliable product identity so licence counts are right.
claims.note: None of the readable sources mentions product identity for licence counting; the ISO 19770-1 page, the one plausibly relevant source, is unreachable (403 to every fetcher, see coverage).

claims.claim: Source signals: SWID, add/remove programs, package managers, file signatures, service names.
claims.note: The only SWID mention (NTIA) calls SWID one of three SBOM formats, not a recognition source signal; no fetched page lists add/remove programs, package managers, file signatures or service names as discovery signals.

claims.claim: Match to a catalogue (vendor-provided recognition library or in-house) producing publisher, product, edition, version.
claims.note: No fetched page describes matching install strings to a recognition catalogue producing publisher, product, edition and version; the SPDX and CycloneDX pages fetched are format overviews with no such process.

claims.claim: Maintain override rules for unmatched items; review the top unrecognised list weekly.
claims.note: 'override rules', 'unrecognised' and any review cadence appear in none of the fetched pages.

claims.claim: Exclude free components (runtimes, drivers) via rule groups.
claims.note: No fetched page covers excluding free runtimes or drivers via rule groups; the GPL FAQ's 'runtime library' and 'driver' mentions are about GPL licensing questions, not ITAM exclusion rules.

claims.claim: Editions (Standard vs Enterprise) can look identical in installed names; use feature flags or licence keys.
claims.note: No fetched page discusses Standard vs Enterprise edition identification, feature flags or licence keys; 'edition' appears only in unrelated newsletter/2019-edition link text.
No fetched page mentions vendors renaming products after acquisitions; NTIA's 'acquisition' hits are about consumers acquiring software.

claims.claim: Verify: recognition rate exceeds 95% on licensable titles.
claims.note: The 95% recognition-rate threshold and 'licensable titles' appear in no fetched source; no page states any recognition-rate target.

coverage: I took every sentence of the skill body - the goal line, all four method bullets, both gotchas and the verify threshold - so every behaviour, signal type and number (the 95% rate) is covered, and checked each against all eight listed sources fetched today: seven fetched fine (spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/ serves a 374-byte JavaScript-redirect stub and reuse.software/spec/ a 270-byte meta-refresh stub to plain fetchers, so neither carries specification content), while iso.org/standard/68291.html returns 403 to every fetcher tried (the web fetch tool twice, urllib with attest.py's wavefront-attest/1 user agent, default Python UA, a browser UA and curl), so it could not be read, hashed or listed in sources; none of the readable pages - SBOM-format overviews (SPDX, CycloneDX, NTIA), open-source licence pages (OSI, GNU GPL FAQ, REUSE) and OpenChain's compliance-program page - mentions software recognition, normalisation, recognition catalogues, override rules, recognition rates or licence counting.
suggested_edits: All 8 claims are unverifiable: the listed sources are SBOM-format, open-source-licence and compliance-program pages, none of which covers ITAM recognition or normalisation practice, and the one plausibly relevant source (ISO/IEC 19770-1 at iso.org/standard/68291.html) is 403 to every fetcher in this environment (it would also break re-fetch checks if cited). A fix PR should bump version and either cite sources that actually describe the practice - ISO/IEC 19770-2 for SWID tags as a source signal, vendor recognition-library documentation (e.g. Flexera, Snow, ServiceNow ITAM) or an ITAM Body of Knowledge for catalogue matching, override rules, excluding free components, edition differentiation and a recognition-rate benchmark for the 95% target - or trim the method/gotchas/verify sections to what such sources support.
